links.outcome: Triage agreement (QWK) and accuracy with RAG grounding versus prompt-only LLM
links.effect: MECR-RAG mean QWK 0.902 vs 0.801 baseline; accuracy 0.802 vs 0.542 (both P<.001); overtriage 28.8% to 12.7%.
links.quote: Across 5 independent runs, MECR‑RAG achieved a mean QWK of 0.902 (SD 0.0021; 95% CI 0.901-0.904), compared with 0.801 (SD 0.004; 95% CI 0.798-0.804) for the baseline model (mean paired difference 0.101, SD 0.0058; 95% CI 0.097-0.106; P <.001).

links.outcome: Sensitivity for high-severity patients, LLM versus initial nurse triage and baseline LLM
links.effect: MECR-RAG sensitivity for R1+R2 124/130 (95.4%) vs nurses 117/130 (90.0%) (P=.02) and baseline LLM 122/130 (93.8%); specificity similar to nurses.
links.quote: When high-severity outcomes were defined as R1+R2 (n=130) and triage “positive” as categories 1 - 3 versus 4 - 5, MECR‑RAG achieved the highest sensitivity for high-risk courses at 124/130 (95.4%), compared with 117/130 (90.0%) for initial nurse triage and 122/130 (93.8%) for the baseline LLM.

links.outcome: Reference standard creation with blinded raters and adjudication; interrater agreement
links.effect: Two blinded advanced practice nurses labelled cases with a third adjudicating disagreements; interrater QWK 0.887.
links.quote: Disagreements were adjudicated by a third senior triage nurse to obtain a final consensus category for each encounter.

links.outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and across LLM backends
links.effect: Five independent runs gave QWK SD 0.0021 for MECR-RAG; advantage robust to run-to-run variability; single-run gains on Claude 3.7 (0.840 to 0.890) and GPT-4o (0.778 to 0.890).
links.quote: Similar effect sizes were observed when analyses were repeated using single median‑run prediction sets, indicating that MECR‑RAG’s advantage was robust to run‑to‑run variability.

links.outcome: Whether standalone performance reflects human-AI team performance and automation bias
links.effect: Authors state usability, automation bias and workflow impact were not evaluated; offline retrospective study cannot show real-world effectiveness or safety.
links.quote: In addition, we did not directly evaluate usability, interpretability, automation bias, or workflow impact, which are increasingly recognized as critical determinants of the safety and effectiveness of AI‑enabled clinical decision-support systems [ 32 , 36 ].

links.outcome: Undertriage and overtriage of urgent cases by LLM triage
links.effect: MECR-RAG undertriage 3/236 (1.3%) vs baseline 4/236 (1.7%); overtriage fell from 68/236 (28.8%) to 30/236 (12.7%) (McNemar P<.001).
links.quote: Overtriage decreased from 68/236 (28.8%) with the baseline LLM to 30/236 (12.7%) with MECR‑RAG (McNemar P <.001).
